title: Browser virtual camera and microphone
summary: On the validated openSUSE test host the v4l2loopback camera appeared as /dev/video0; the audio server identified PulseAudio on PipeWire 1.6.9, with null sink service_audio and remapped source service_mic. Firefox captured earlier test media; the dev3 native package has not been live-device retested.
invariants: Do not assume /dev/video42; the observed camera in this development session is /dev/video0.
Start the media producer before browser camera discovery when exclusive_caps is active.
Never assume a VLC v4l2:///dev/video0 preview includes audio; select service_mic in a microphone-aware application.
Do not redirect other host audio streams to the service sink accidentally.
A browser displaying a camera preview is not evidence that a WhatsApp recipient received audio or video.
procedure: Confirm pactl info reports the PipeWire PulseAudio compatibility server.
Confirm /dev/video0 is the intended virtual camera and not the laptop's hardware camera.
Confirm service_audio exists as a sink, service_mic as its remapped monitor source, and verify per-application microphone selection.
Qualify on Firefox and Chromium separately using real receiver-side capture.

provenance.claim: openSUSE V4L2/PipeWire prerequisites and user-selection procedure.
